$comment: DECLARED — THE ROSETTA STONE OVERRIDE. knownDevices.json says what a MODEL is;
this file says what the instrument AT A PLACE is, when it cannot say so itself.
Discovery asks *IDN? and believes the answer. A box that never answers (the HP 3235
switch matrix takes commands and replies to none) or answers with no serial (four
HP 34401A meters all say serial 0) cannot identify itself, so a PERSON identifies
it, here, hard-written and in git — never guessed by software, never by IP alone.
Each key is a LOCATOR, the place the VISA plugin sees the instrument, most specific
first: a USB adapter's serial, a USB port path (1-6.2), a tty name (ttyUSB0), or the
VISA resource exactly (TCPIP::<gateway>::gpib7,10::INSTR; TCPIP0:: is the same board).
Each value:
model         a key of knownDevices.json — what it IS (manufacturer, type, panel,
commands and the hourly self-test follow from it). Optional when the
instrument names itself and only lacks a serial: then only the tag.
tag           its asset tag, filed as its serial when it has none of its own (the
role config.ini [visa] asset_tags had; that key still layers on top
for a bench that is not this checkout).
declared_by / declared_at   who said so, and when (ISO 8601).
note          why — what the person knows that the bus cannot.
network       for a network locator (TCPIP::…), the CIDR its host sits inside —
the rule bench.json holds every addressed row to (PLAN-815.01).
confirmed_by / confirmed_at  a person who looked and said 'OK, got it'.
A declaration never overrules an instrument that DOES answer: if *IDN? names another
model, the instrument is believed and the disagreement is raised loudly (problem
declaration_mismatch). A declared box that does not answer is shown as DECLARED, never
as verified. The Discovery page writes here (Declare…, OK got it); a change it makes
is a working-tree edit and must be committed to count.

TCPIP::44.44.44.222::gpib7,10::INSTR.note: Owner, 2026-11-05: 'with 100% certainty this is 10 … the declaration of GPIB 10 is a switcher.' The HP 3235 switch matrix behind the E5810 at 44.44.44.222: it takes commands and answers none, *IDN? included, so no scan can name it.
